correctness.rationale: Direct derivation proves the Fourier–Bessel formula, Bessel energy derivative E'=2xJ0², its strict inequality at each Fourier root, and the resulting same-orientation crossing uniqueness in each J0 gap. The implicit derivative of x_n and strict increase of qx_n from 0 to j_(0,n) prove exactly n-1 critical points with explicit coordinates and alternating nonzero curvature. The endpoint expansions use locally uniform convergence plus the implicit-function theorem. A standalone checker completed 84 roots, 66 critical points and 24 endpoint sanity checks, supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The exact positive-root simplicity and gap uniqueness are derived for J1(x)-qJ1(qx), and the main new all-n result counts n-1 nondegenerate stationary points of each zero branch. Related Bessel zero interlacing, annular optics endpoint formulas, and annular Laplacian J/Y cross-product asymptotics were materially compared. The closest inspected claims do not imply the all-parameter Fourier-zero trajectory census; a full literature priority determination remains a documented risk.

Search-result absence cannot establish publication priority. All scientific comparisons are same-author-level review, not independent verification.

value.rationale: The annular aperture is a canonical Fourier/Hankel object. The all-ring gap uniqueness and exact n-1 nondegenerate turning points, rising without bound with ring index, solve a natural infinite-family structural question in diffraction-zero geometry. The monotone first ring, increasingly nonmonotone higher rings, and computable extremal parameters are useful precise facts absent from the compared endpoint-only literature; no inflated downstream consequence is claimed.
